newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm after spot slides.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm after spot slides.

text.p: Escalating talk of concerted central bank intervention lifted volatilities on dollar/yen options in U.S. trading as the spot was knocked below 125 yen for the first time since early April.
The dollar's fall came overnight after the Kyodo News Agency said Japan, the United States and Germany were mulling a joint effort to sell dollars for yen to stem further yen weakness.
Corporate interest in hedging dollar positions picked up noticeably this week and was continuing this morning, options traders and analysts said.
"Most dealers are reporting a lot of corporate demand for downside protection," said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.

Steady buying of out-of-the-money dollar puts and yen calls in durations of one month and less characterized activity, with the unbalanced demand sharpening the yen call risk-reversal skew, analysts said.

Risk reversals, the put-call pricing differential, favored yen calls 0.5/0.7 for one-month 25-delta options. Yen call buyers were seen paying 0.5 on several hundred thousand dollars worth of risk reversals Tuesday and 0.6 today.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen gained about 0.15 point from the previous session to 8.65/8.85 percent. One-year firmed slightly to 9.40/9.55 percent.
Yet analysts for the most part were unconvinced that a coordinated move by the so-called Group of Three (G3) was in the cards while the dollar coasts to levels considered more reasonable.

"The market is taking care of itself," Revercomb said. "G3 and G7 have made it clear what they want with the dollar -- low volatility and a lower dollar. They're not likely to intervene here as long as the dollar is behaving well."

Market participants said good corporate and hedge fund bidding interest around the lows at 124.50-60 yen suggested support at 124 would remain intact, though another test of 124.50 could raise anxiety levels.
Conversely, volatilities would be expected to ease on any return to 126 yen, analysts said.
The dollar was bid at 124.91 yen around midday.
The market's focus on dollar/yen overshadowed dollar/mark, where volatilities were little changed with the spot placid near 1.72.
One-month implied volatility was 8.45/8.65 percent, down 0.05 point, and one-year also declined marginally to 9.05/9.15 percent. Risk reversals retained a slight bias toward mark puts.
